thread.title: Top Stocks Today: Arbor Realty In Sweet Spot Of Growth | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Top Stocks Today: Arbor Realty In Sweet Spot Of Growth | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Top stocks today in the technology sector aren't easy to find as FANG stocks like Apple ( AAPL ), Amazon.com ( AMZN ) and Netflix ( NFLX ) face increased selling pressure. But selling in the technology sector has spawned opportunities in other areas of the market, particularly in stocks that pay dividends.
X Arbor Realty Trust ( ABR ) is one of the top stocks today in the real estate investment trusts (REIT) space. It invests in a diversified portfolio of multifamily and commercial real estate loans, preferred equity investments and mortgage-related securities.
Top Stocks Today: Healthy Dividends Arbor Realty pays a quarterly dividend of 25 cents a share, giving it a big annualized dividend yield of just over 8%. It's a tempting yield, no doubt, but in the mortgage REIT space, juicy dividend yields are the rule. Keep in mind, though, that during periods of economic weakness, mortgage REITs are particularly vulnerable because the loans they invest in can sour quickly.
When the recession hit in 2008, shares of Arbor Realty fell hard, from a high of 19.20 at the end of 2007 to a low of 56 cents at the end of March 2009.
Top Stocks Today: Healthy Fundamentals Fast-forward to today, and times are good for Arbor Realty and other mortgage REITs. Shares have perked up on the heels of the company's earnings report last week.
Funds from operations jumped 48% to 37 cents a share. Revenue growth accelerated for the third straight quarter, rising 37% to $123.1 million.
In terms of its technical health, Arbor Realty has been trading tightly near highs as it works on a base with a 12.45 entry. Major indexes ended with losses Friday, but Arbor Realty jumped nearly 3% in higher volume.
Headed into Monday, the mortgage REIT industry group was working on a five-session win streak. It outperformed again in afternoon trading Monday, up another 0.6%.
